The patient presents with dysuria (painful urination), urinary frequency (feeling the need to go all the time), cloudy urine, and foul-smelling urine. These are hallmark clinical features of a lower urinary tract infection (cystitis). Among the provided options, urinary tract infection is the only condition that aligns with these specific genitourinary symptoms. Other conditions like diabetes might cause frequent urination but typically present with polydipsia and weight loss rather than painful, cloudy, and foul-smelling urine.
